input: Find bribery and corruption cases involving Trafigura

entity.group: Trafigura Group — employee-owned commodities trading group; subsidiaries include Puma Energy, Nyrstar, Impala Terminals, Galena Asset Management, Greenergy
entity.legal_name: Trafigura Group Pte. Ltd. (current group holding; relevant conduct period parent: Trafigura Beheer B.V.)

events.date: Scheme ~2003–2014; DOJ information filed 13 Dec 2023; guilty plea/resolution 28 Mar 2024
events.type: Bribery of foreign public officials (FCPA conspiracy) — bribes to Petrobras officials, concealed via shell companies and offshore accounts
events.amount: ~USD 19.7 million in bribes; ~USD 61 million profit; criminal fine USD 80,488,040 + forfeiture USD 46,510,257 + USD 400 assessment (up to USD 26,829,346 credited against Brazilian payments)
events.status: Settled/convicted — Trafigura Beheer B.V. entered a guilty-plea resolution; DOJ case status 'Resolved'; DOJ stated the resolution closes its Trafigura investigation; 3-year enhanced-compliance self-reporting, no independent monitor
events.parties: Trafigura Beheer B.V. (former parent of Trafigura Group); Singapore subsidiary Trafigura Pte. Ltd. named as involved entity; DOJ Fraud Section and U.S. Attorney's Office S.D. Fla.
events.summary: US DOJ resolved a single-count FCPA antibribery conspiracy charge over Trafigura's decade-long scheme paying up to 20 cents per barrel in bribes to Petrobras officials to win oil-products business.

events.date: Resolution announced 31 Mar 2025 (press statement); reported 1 Apr 2025
events.type: Corruption/bribery — civil and administrative settlement with Brazilian authorities over the Petrobras bribery scheme
events.amount: USD 76 million total per press report; Trafigura statement: additional USD 49 million (~BRL 282 million) paid to the Brazilian government, with up to USD 26.8 million credited under the March 2024 DOJ agreement
events.status: Settled — resolves civil cases brought by CGU (Comptroller General), AGU (Attorney General) and MPF (Federal Prosecutors); Trafigura states it closes Brazilian authorities' investigation
events.parties: Trafigura Beheer B.V. (former parent of Trafigura Group) with the Brazilian CGU, AGU and MPF
events.summary: Trafigura settled with Brazilian enforcement authorities, paying an additional USD 49 million (total ~USD 76 million reported) to close the civil side of the Petrobras bribery probe, following the 2024 US DOJ resolution on the same facts.

events.date: Administrative liability proceeding instituted 31 Dec 2020 (Portaria 3.093/2020); final CGU report recommending sanctions; conduct 2009–2014
events.type: Administrative corruption enforcement (Brazil Law 12.846/2013) — undue advantage given to a Petrobras public agent and associated money laundering
events.amount: CGU recommended fine of R$ 47,363,207,512.84 against Trafigura Pte. Ltd. and R$ 518,417.10 against Trafigura do Brasil Consultoria Ltda.; bribes to Petrobras manager Marcus Alcoforado of USD 1,292,400 across 31 spot fuel-oil contracts (May 2012–Sep 2013)
events.status: Recommended sanctions in final CGU (Corregedoria) report; foreign entities that did not appear declared contumacious; matter ultimately resolved by the 2025 settlements with CGU/AGU/MPF
events.parties: Trafigura Pte. Ltd., Trafigura Beheer B.V., Trafigura do Brasil Consultoria Ltda. and Trafigura do Brasil Importação, Exportação e Comércio Ltda. (solidary liability recommended); intermediaries Mariano Marcondes Ferraz and Marcio Pinto de Magalhães
events.summary: Brazil's Comptroller General (CGU, Operação Sem Limites, 57th Lava Jato phase) found Trafigura representatives, with the acquiescence of late founder Claude Dauphin, paid bribes to a Petrobras contracts manager, with funds laundered via doleiros, and recommended massive administrative fines; settled in 2025.

events.type: Criminal charges — active corruption, passive corruption and money laundering
events.status: Charged / ongoing criminal prosecution per CGU final report (latest status available in corpus)
events.parties: Former Trafigura executives Mariano Marcondes Ferraz and Marcio Pinto de Magalhães, ex-Petrobras manager Marcus Antonio Pacheco Alcoforado and financial operator Carlos Herz
events.summary: Brazilian federal prosecutors in Curitiba charged two former Trafigura executives, a Petrobras manager and a financial operator with corruption and money laundering over the Petrobras bribe scheme; Herz's case was split into a separate action (no. 5035910-39.2019.4.04.7000).

events.date: Indictment filed 5 Dec 2023; investigation opened Jul 2020; conduct Apr 2009–Oct 2011
events.type: Bribery of foreign public officials (Art. 322septies Swiss Criminal Code) — company charged with failing to take reasonable organisational measures to prevent bribery
events.amount: Bribes of EUR 4,346,176.60 in bank transfers to a Geneva account + USD 604,000 in cash in Angola (plus CHF 797.25 expenses); alleged group profits USD 143.7 million from 8 ship-chartering and 1 bunkering contract with Sonangol Distribuidora
events.parties: Trafigura Beheer B.V. (then parent company), its former COO (Mike Wainwright), a former Trafigura intermediary/employee, and a former CEO of Sonangol Distribuidora SA
events.summary: Switzerland's Office of the Attorney General indicted Trafigura Beheer B.V. and three individuals for foreign-bribery offenses over payments to a former Sonangol official to win Angolan oil-related contracts — the first time the Swiss Federal Criminal Court was asked to judge a company's liability for bribing foreign officials.
events.jurisdiction: Switzerland — Office of the Attorney General / Federal Criminal Court

events.type: Bribery of foreign public officials — corporate and individual conviction
events.amount: Company: CHF 3 million fine (~USD 3.3 million) plus ~USD 145 million (USD 145.6 million reported) set aside for compensation claims; prosecutors had sought over USD 156 million; Wainwright: 32-month prison sentence, 12 months to be served
events.status: Convicted — verdict not final; Trafigura's lawyers said the company and Wainwright intend to appeal
events.parties: Trafigura (via Trafigura Beheer B.V.) and former COO Mike Wainwright; also convicted: a former high-level Trafigura employee acting as intermediary and a former Sonangol official
events.summary: Switzerland's Federal Criminal Court in Bellinzona convicted Trafigura and three individuals of bribery over ~USD 5 million in payments to an Angolan oil official that secured ~USD 144 million in contracts — the first Swiss corporate conviction for bribing a foreign official at the Federal Criminal Court.

output.assessment: Trafigura carries a high, now largely crystallised foreign-bribery risk profile: within twelve months (2024–2025) it absorbed a US DOJ guilty plea (~USD 127 million) over the Petrobras bribery scheme, ~USD 76 million in Brazilian civil/administrative settlements, and Switzerland's first corporate foreign-bribery conviction (CHF 3 million fine plus ~USD 145 million compensation set aside), alongside the criminal conviction of its former COO Mike Wainwright. Group-wide enforcement exposure on these two schemes (Brazil and Angola) is therefore substantially closed and quantified, but the announced Swiss appeals and the ongoing Curitiba criminal case against former executives remain open. Separately, a 2023 nickel-fraud loss (~USD 577 million, later recouped via ~USD 700 million in court-awarded damages against Prateek Gupta) and a 2024 USD 1.1 billion Mongolia writedown over manipulated data — while victim-side rather than bribery matters — indicate recurring internal-control weaknesses that sustained monitoring should weigh.
missing_fields: Outcome of the announced appeals against the 31 January 2025 Swiss conviction (Trafigura and Mike Wainwright) — no ruling found as of 10 November 2026
Current status/outcome of the Curitiba criminal prosecution of former Trafigura executives (case 5058533-34.2018.404.7000) after the CGU final report — no later ruling found

excluded_namesakes.name: Jeffrey Tesler (US DOJ oil-services bribery cases)
excluded_namesakes.reason: Tesler appears in DOJ oil-bribery materials surfaced by Trafigura searches, but those cases concern his role in the KBR/TSKJ Nigeria LNG bribery scheme; the pages show no Trafigura involvement, so they were excluded from Trafigura events.

excluded_namesakes.name: Odebrecht Dutch conduit money-laundering prosecution (Dutch OM, March 2026)
excluded_namesakes.reason: A Dutch OM case over ~EUR 200 million funnelled for Odebrecht via Dutch companies surfaced in Trafigura bribery searches; it concerns Odebrecht and two Dutchmen, not Trafigura.

excluded_namesakes.name: Trafigura Beheer B.V. / Trafigura Pte. Ltd. / Trafigura do Brasil
excluded_namesakes.reason: Not excluded as namesakes: these are entities of the same Trafigura group (Beheer B.V. was the group's parent during the relevant period; Pte. Ltd. is the current Singapore parent), so they are included as parties in the events above.
